Installation & setup

Source: vignettes/installation.Rmd
installation.Rmd

This guide gets shadshiny installed and a first app running, and explains how it sits alongside Shiny, Bootstrap and bslib.

Install

shadshiny is not yet on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub with any of:

# pak (recommended)
pak::pak("orijitghosh/shadshiny")

# remotes
remotes::install_github("orijitghosh/shadshiny")

There is no build step — no npm, no Node, no bundler. All CSS and JavaScript ship precompiled inside the package as a single htmlDependency().

Your first app

Wrap the UI in page_shad() and use components like any other Shiny tag. Bound components take an inputId and read back through input$<id>.

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

ui <- page_shad(
  theme_preset = "violet",
  shad_card(
    shad_card_header(shad_card_title("Hello, shadshiny")),
    shad_card_content(
      shad_input("name", label = "Your name", placeholder = "Ada"),
      shad_button("greet", "Say hi")
    ),
    shad_card_footer(textOutput("out"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$out <- renderText({
    req(input$greet)
    paste0("Hi, ", input$name, "!")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

What page_shad() does

page_shad() is the only wrapper you need. It:

  • attaches the shadshiny asset bundle (tokens, base CSS, runtime JS, every component’s CSS/JS, and the Shiny binding layer, in the correct order);
  • establishes a .shad-scope root and applies your theme_preset;
  • sets dark mode when you pass dark = TRUE/FALSE, or follows bslib/OS when dark = NULL (the default).

Under the hood it builds on bslib::page_fillable() when bslib is installed, and falls back to shiny::fluidPage() otherwise. Everything a normal Shiny page accepts still works.

page_shad(
  title = "My app",         # browser tab title
  theme_preset = "blue",    # one of the seven presets
  dark = NULL,              # NULL = follow bslib/OS; TRUE/FALSE to force
  # ... your UI ...
)

Coexisting with Bootstrap & bslib

shadshiny is designed to layer on top of an existing Bootstrap 5 / bslib app rather than replace it:

  • Every shad rule is class-scoped (.shad-*) and unlayered, so it neither leaks into Bootstrap components nor gets overridden by Reboot.
  • Colours are namespaced custom properties (--shad-*), so they never collide with Bootstrap variables.
  • Dark mode listens for [data-bs-theme="dark"], which is exactly what bslib::input_dark_mode() toggles — so one switch drives both systems.

That means you can drop shadshiny components into an existing dashboard incrementally. If you’re already inside a bslib page and don’t want the page_shad() wrapper, attach the assets manually with shadshiny_deps():

library(bslib)
library(shadshiny)

page_sidebar(
  shadshiny_deps(),                 # attach the bundle once, up front
  sidebar = sidebar("Filters"),
  shad_card(shad_card_content("A shad card inside a bslib page."))
)

Running the examples

The package ships eight runnable example apps that together exercise the whole library. List and launch them with shad_run_example():

shad_run_example("kitchen-sink")        # every component, one page
shad_run_example("02-analytics-dashboard")

Calling shad_run_example() with an unknown name prints the available example directories.
